Build the area to tessellate within, from points or a boundary

Source: R/tessellation.R
clip_target_for.Rd

Builds the area that the hex and square cells of build_tessellation() are clipped to. With a boundary it is that boundary, row for row; without one it is the axis-aligned bounding box of points_sf in the working CRS. Either can be buffered by expand.

Usage

clip_target_for(points_sf, boundary = NULL, expand = 0, quiet = FALSE)

Arguments

points_sf

An sf object with POINT/MULTIPOINT geometry. Points that mix XY and XYZ (or XYM), or that carry M, are read in x and y, since sf reads a layer in the dimension of its first geometry and GEOS refuses M. A point that is empty, or has a coordinate that is not finite or lies beyond 1e150, has no location and takes no part in the bounding box. With no boundary, points none of which has a location (as given, or after the move of lon/lat points into a projected CRS) are refused with an error that says so. Points that take the buffer, so far from the origin of their CRS that doubles there are spaced more than a millionth of the target's size apart (0.125 at 1e15, beside a disk of radius 1), give a buffer drawn at that rounding, with a warning of class "spatialkit_xy_imprecise" that gives the spacing and the radius. Where the buffer comes back empty or with no area, as a radius below that spacing can make it, the call stops with an error of class "spatialkit_xy_imprecise_error". Shift such points nearer the origin, or pass boundary.

boundary

Optional polygonal sf object. One with no CRS, given with points that have one, is interpreted in the points' own CRS, with a warning. With points in a projected CRS it is read as harmonize_crs() does: coordinates that look like lon/lat are taken as EPSG:4326 and reprojected, anything else is stamped with the points' CRS. With lon/lat points it is read as lon/lat when its coordinates fit the lon/lat envelope, and refused with an error otherwise. Rows without a location, rows the repair leaves without a polygon, vertices at a latitude beyond 90 and mixed dimensions are handled as "Boundaries" in spatialkit-geometry says.

expand

A single non-negative number. Below 1 it is a fraction of the longer side of the bounding box (of boundary when one is given, otherwise of points_sf); 1 or more is a distance in the units of the CRS the target is built in. Default 0 (no buffer). Lon/lat input is first projected to a local projected CRS (see Value), so both forms are in that CRS's units.

quiet

Logical; suppress this function's progress message()s. It does not silence R warnings, nor the package's console log echo (see spatialkit_quiet for that). Default FALSE.

Value

An sf polygon layer representing the clip target. For lon/lat input the layer is returned in the automatically selected local projected CRS, not the input CRS; a message reports this unless quiet = TRUE.

Details

Use it to build the boundary that method = "hex" and "square" require, to check that a study-area polygon contains the observations before tessellating, or to pass the same envelope to create_voronoi_polygons() and create_grid_polygons() so that two tessellations of one dataset cover the same ground.

It is not the target build_tessellation() derives on its own: method = "voronoi" without a boundary clips to the convex hull of the points (or of their cover, for seeds) buffered by 2 percent of its diagonal, and there expand is always a distance. A bounding box over a non-rectangular point cloud includes corners with no data, so a hex or square grid laid over it has cells that hold no points; pass the study-area polygon when there is one.

Points with no extent

Points that all share one x or one y, or nearly so (the short side of their bounding box below a millionth of the long side, or below about 1.5e-154, a length whose square doubles cannot hold), get a small buffer around them instead of a box. When every point sits at one location, or the share of their spread the buffer would take (5 percent, or a fractional expand) is below that length, the box has no extent to take a share of, and the target is a disk of radius 1 unit of the CRS around it (1 m in a metre CRS, 1 km in a kilometre CRS), unless expand is 1 or more, which is then the radius; the message says so. Pass boundary for a target of real size.

See also

Other cell building: build_tessellation(), create_grid_polygons(), create_grid_polygons_cached(), create_voronoi_polygons(), ensure_stable_poly_id(), get_voronoi_seeds(), plot_tessellation_map(), voronoi_seeds_kmeans(), voronoi_seeds_random()

Examples

library(sf)
set.seed(1)
pts <- st_as_sf(
  data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(30, 0, 100), y = 5e6 + runif(30, 0, 100)),
  coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632
)
# No boundary: the bounding box, expanded by 10% of the extent
box <- clip_target_for(pts, expand = 0.1, quiet = TRUE)
st_area(box)
#> 12054.18 [m^2]
